corpus.note: Every count below was re-run against this shelf on 2026-08-28. The source surface (cr_scratch/step0_space_resources_engineer_question_surface.md section 3) was written against the 158-file pre-merge lsei/literature tree and four of its ten absence claims have moved. Each entry carries a reverify field saying which.

rule.name: R3 - refuse by substitution, not by apology
rule.statement: A question landing in a thin patch does not answer from the nearest word-overlap match and does not say the corpus is limited. It names the specific missing measurement, then names the nearest real evidence and what that evidence is instead. Shorter than the apology, and it tells the reader what to go and find.
rule.bad: the literature in this corpus is limited on the geotechnical properties of icy regolith
rule.good: No measurement of icy-regolith shear strength or cone penetration resistance at permanently shadowed region temperature exists in this corpus. The nearest evidence is Barnett 2025 on regolith consolidation during thaw, which is the opposite process.
rule.refusal_code_note: not-found is the correct code for every entry here: no address resolved and no shelf file confirmed for the specific measurement. Where the app also declares the topic excluded, not-found is still written, because excluded routes to nobody and must never mask a code that routes to someone (answer_contract.md section 5).

firing_rule.name: trigger mass, IDF-weighted, lunar-scoped
firing_rule.why: A COUNT RULE OVER TRIGGER TOKENS DOES NOT WORK AND A MASS RULE DOES. Under any-token-fires, T1 fires on SRQ-7 on the single token 'regolith' (idf 0.662) and T2 fires on SRQ-13 on 'bearing' (1.411). Both are correct vocabulary and wrong triggers on their own. Measured by The Engineer at W4-3 and re-measured here on a wider control set.
firing_rule.score: mass = sum over the patch's trigger_tokens present in the question's tokens of idfFor('literature','lunar',token). tokenize() and idfFor() are both exported from oracle/retrieval/literature_search.js; this needs no new mechanism.
firing_rule.two_tiers: FIRING IS NOT GOVERNING, and conflating them is what makes a single threshold fail. A patch that FIRES attaches its `substitution` to the answer as content. A patch that GOVERNS makes its `refusal_code` the verdict. T3 fires on SRQ-10 at 5.961 and SRQ-10 is BOTH -- the acceptance row says so in its own Must-carry cell. A one-tier rule has to choose between silencing that legitimate fire and turning a BOTH into a REFUSE.

fire_threshold.evidence: below the band: T1 on SRQ-7 and on SRQ-5, both 0.662 on 'regolith' alone, the false fire this rule exists to stop; and T2's own probe_neg at 1.478. Above it: T10 on SRQ-7 at 1.858, which is a CORRECT fire -- SRQ-7's Must-carry cell already requires the May 2025 date T10 supplies.

govern_threshold.evidence: must govern: SRQ-13/T1 8.540, SRQ-14/T5 6.389, and all ten probe_pos rows at 10.238 or above. Must not govern: SRQ-10/T3 5.961 (verdict BOTH), LCC-14 probe_pos/T6 5.601 (verdict CONTESTED), and the ten probe_neg rows at 5.550 or below. Separates all 49 labelled questions.
govern_threshold.margin_warning: The band is 0.428 wide, about 7 percent. It is real and it separates every row measured, but it is tight, and the row constraining it from below (T3 on SRQ-10) is a LEGITIMATE fire rather than a false one. That is the single-threshold design at its limit and it is the argument for the two tiers above.

firing_rule.owner: The threshold values are PROVISIONAL and are the router seat's to set, on the same footing as K in oracle/router/axis_threshold.json. What is authored here is the rule, the labelled fixture set (probe_pos/probe_neg per patch), and the measured bands. Re-measure with cr_scratch/sre_w4/tp_band2.js and tp_probemass.js.
firing_rule.refuted: The Engineer's W4-3 proposal of any threshold in (1.86, 3.78] is REFUTED by the wider control set. That band was measured on five rows and contained neither SRQ-10 nor the LCC-14 probe_pos. A threshold of 2.5 or 3.0 makes T3 govern SRQ-10 and T6 govern LCC-14, flipping a BOTH and a CONTESTED into REFUSE. The shape of the finding stands; the number does not.
firing_rule.precondition_refuted: An obvious-looking precondition -- let a patch govern only where no competing route answered -- is REFUTED by measurement. SRQ-13 returns LITERATURE confirmed 9 of 9 at frac 0.85, so that precondition would block T1 on exactly the row it must govern. A confirmed retrieval is not evidence the question was answered; that is the whole content of the third failure mode The Engineer identified.
firing_rule.token_form: Every trigger token satisfies tokenize(t) deep-equals [t]. Nine did not before this repair and could never match: 'boil-off' (T5), 'MTBF' (T3), 'he-3' 'helium-3' 'REE' 'KREEP' 'PGM' (T7), 'TRL' and 'as of' (T10). The defect class is wider than the hyphen: uppercase and multi-word forms fail identically, and 'as of' tokenizes to nothing at all because both halves are stopwords. Check with cr_scratch/sre_w4/fix_triggers.js.
firing_rule.no_corpus_floor: The corpus-presence floor asserted on excluded-node match_keys DOES NOT APPLY HERE, and applying it would be backwards. A thin patch exists because a measurement is absent, so a trigger naming that measurement is expected to be absent from the corpus: 'shear' (T1), 'tribology' and 'ingress' (T2) occur in no summary on this shelf. Their absence is evidence the patch is real, not evidence the trigger is wrong.
firing_rule.kept_deliberately: T1 keeps 'regolith' and T2 keeps 'bearing'. Both are correct vocabulary for their patch and both contribute to a true positive: 'regolith' is 0.662 of T1's 8.540 on SRQ-13 and 'bearing' is 1.411 of it. The mass rule is what makes them safe, and removing them would lower the true-positive signal to fix a problem the rule already fixes.

patches.title: Icy-regolith geotechnics
patches.rank_basis: ask-frequency times how confidently the corpus would answer wrongly
patches.probe_pos: What shear strength and cone penetration resistance does frozen icy regolith have when you dig it?
patches.probe_neg: Which review paper surveys lunar regolith excavation concepts?
patches.absent: Shear strength, bearing capacity, cone penetration resistance and specific excavation force for ice-bearing regolith at permanently shadowed region temperature. No measurement of any of the four exists in this corpus.
patches.reverify: HOLDS. All four absence greps still return zero against the 169-file shelf. One change: 'excavation force' now returns one file, just-2020, which reviews the concept and reports no measurement.

nearest_evidence.what: regolith consolidation caused by thawing of water ice - the opposite process, and a single IAC paper
thirteen excavation concepts reviewed; the paper's own output is recommendations for experiments not yet performed
lunar TBMs, explicitly conceptual, no original experimental or design data
NASA's own framework for architecture-driven data gaps; establishes that the agency documents this class of absence rather than holding the measurement

patches.substitution: No measurement of icy-regolith shear strength, bearing capacity, cone penetration resistance or specific excavation force at PSR temperature exists in this corpus. The nearest evidence is Barnett 2025 on regolith consolidation during thaw, which is the opposite process, and Just 2020, whose own conclusion is a list of excavation experiments not yet performed.

undermines.how: kExc = 4 t regolith/yr per t plant sets the entire mass-bound regime. Nothing in the corpus constrains it and nothing in the corpus can.

patches.title: Dust, abrasion and wear
patches.probe_pos: What abrasive wear rate and seal life should I assume for a duty cycle on dusty lunar machinery?
patches.probe_neg: Which programme documents name dust mitigation as an architecture need?
patches.absent: Abrasive wear rates, bearing and seal life, and tribology under vacuum with regolith ingress. Nothing in this corpus measures how long lunar surface machinery runs before it stops.
patches.reverify: HOLDS, unchanged. All three wear greps still zero; dust mitigation still three files, and all three are programme documents rather than wear measurements.

nearest_evidence.what: names dust mitigation as an architecture need; carries no wear rate
same, at the base-design level
a community newsletter reporting activity, not a measurement
states explicitly that wear and mission risk from tanker traverse frequency are discussed qualitatively only and are not quantified in the model

patches.substitution: No wear rate, bearing life or seal life for lunar surface machinery exists in this corpus. Three files name dust mitigation as a programme need and none measures it. Kleinhenz 2020 is the nearest, and it says in its own words that its model does not quantify wear.

undermines.how: duty = 0.6 is the active-extraction fraction of calendar time. Every annual production figure in the app, and in every architecture study in the corpus, rests on an assumed duty cycle with no wear evidence behind it.

patches.title: Maintenance, reliability and spares
patches.probe_pos: What mtbf and spares provisioning does lunar plant reliability and maintenance require over its life?
patches.probe_neg: What depreciation rate does BEA publish for mining machinery?
patches.absent: Lunar-surface reliability data of any kind. No failure rate, no MTBF and no spares provisioning measured on or for lunar hardware.
patches.reverify: MOVED, narrowed. The source surface said rahimdel-2024 is the only reliability primary. That is refuted: shishko-2019 also carries MTBF, in a lunar thermal-mining business case, which is a closer object than a terrestrial mining truck. The absence itself holds - neither file reports a measured lunar failure rate - but the nearest evidence is nearer than claimed.

nearest_evidence.what: carries MTBF inside a lunar thermal-mining production-rate framework; the paper's own summary states it is not a completed cost or NPV result
Bayesian reliability of terrestrial mining trucks - a real method on the wrong planet
spares and closure at the study level, 1980

patches.substitution: No measured lunar-surface failure rate or MTBF exists in this corpus. Shishko 2019 carries MTBF inside a lunar thermal-mining framework whose own summary says it is not a completed result; Rahimdel 2024 is a real Bayesian reliability study of terrestrial mining trucks.

undermines.how: L = 10 yr is a design assumption. decayRate = 0.15/yr and decayLife = 11 yr are SOURCED, and the source is BEA depreciation for terrestrial mining and oil field machinery. The amortized-plant identity is the app's whole economic engine and its plant-life terms come from Earth. The app says so in its own source string; the answer must too.

patches.title: Water cleanup and downstream contamination
patches.probe_pos: What purity and contaminant removal does water cleanup and purification reach before electrolysis?
patches.probe_neg: At what temperature does molten regolith electrolysis operate?
patches.absent: Any primary reporting cleanup performance - a measured removal fraction, a contaminant specification, or an electrolysis-feed purity achieved from sublimated lunar vapour. The corpus documents that this step is immature without documenting how immature.
patches.reverify: MOVED, and this is the sharpest change. Kleinhenz 2020, which was not on the pre-merge shelf under this heading, states in its own words that water cleanup hardware is not yet defined and is not included in its model because contaminant criteria for the water were still unknown. That is a documented absence with an author and a page, which is a far better substitution than a general claim of thinness. Gott 2024 and Barnett 2025 (volatile exposure limits) also landed and bear on measuring the product stream. The absence of a cleanup performance figure holds.

nearest_evidence.what: states water cleanup hardware is not yet defined and is excluded from the model because contaminant criteria were unknown
the only integrated extract-capture-liquefy demonstration; names volatile contamination and dust mobilisation as unresolved
puts capture and cleanup at TRL 3/4 and notes alkaline electrolysis of dirty water has unresolved corrosion issues (May 2025)
a flight-forward residual gas analyser for quantifying a product gas stream - the instrument, not the cleanup performance
simulation of the volatile mass needed to reach spacecraft exposure limits; contamination as a hazard, not as a process yield

patches.substitution: No measured cleanup removal fraction or electrolysis-feed purity from lunar-derived water exists in this corpus. Kleinhenz 2020 states that its own model excludes cleanup hardware because the contaminant criteria were undefined; Sanders 2025 places capture and cleanup at TRL 3/4 as of May 2025.

undermines.coefficient_status: ASSUMPTION (optimistic bound, no primary reports 100 percent); SOURCED (design target, ahead of demonstration); SOURCED (derived)
undermines.how: Every propellant figure downstream of extraction passes through a step nothing in the corpus measures.

patches.title: Cryogenic fluid management, boil-off and transfer cadence

patches.probe_pos: How often is cryogenic propellant transferred, and what boil-off does a depot tank lose between transfers?
patches.probe_neg: Which paper sizes a cryocooler for lunar liquefaction?
patches.absent: Any primary on lunar-surface cryogenic transfer: a measured transfer loss, a surface boil-off rate, or an operational transfer cadence.
patches.reverify: HOLDS. 'cryogenic transfer' still returns zero. Boil-off and cryocooler files are all modelling terms inside architecture studies rather than surface measurements.

nearest_evidence.what: cryogenic storage and boil-off for a Mars ascent vehicle - the closest real treatment, on the wrong body
sizes a Dust Tolerant Automated Umbilical and cryocooler-based liquefaction with radiator mass; a design model, not a demonstration

patches.substitution: No measurement of lunar-surface cryogenic transfer loss, surface boil-off rate or transfer cadence exists in this corpus. Kleinhenz 2017 treats cryogenic storage and boil-off for a Mars ascent vehicle; Kleinhenz 2020 sizes a dust-tolerant umbilical and cryocooler liquefaction as a design model with no demonstration behind it.

undermines.how: The app excludes this - 'This app does not model programme milestones.' The exclusions matcher requires a topic overlap, and a thin corpus can still produce a word-overlap match, so nothing refuses. The matcher's own header comment names this exact failure as its motivating case. Outcome EXCLUDED-THEN-THIN.

patches.refusal_code_note: not-found, not excluded. The app's boundary is real but excluded routes to nobody, and the fix here is an acquisition decision, which routes to someone.

patches.title: Non-water product routes past oxygen
patches.probe_pos: What energy does smelting iron or refining rare earth and platinum metals from regolith take?
patches.probe_neg: How much helium is implanted in lunar regolith?
patches.absent: An iron production route treated as a primary product rather than an MRE byproduct, with its own energy figure. For helium-3, an operating demand side. For REE and PGM, a lunar ore grade.
patches.reverify: MOVED, and this entry is materially less thin than the source surface claimed. The surface said REE and PGM hold two files, neither lunar-specific in the way a question would need. That is refuted. McLeod 2017 is a lunar-specific REE review that reaches a negative result stated in its own abstract: there is at present no geological, mineralogical or chemical evidence supporting REE concentrations on the Moon that would classify them as ores. Levin 2025 maps crustal KREEP distribution, which is the host. USGS 2025 supplies the terrestrial PGM market side. Iron and the helium-3 demand side are unchanged and still thin.

nearest_evidence.what: lunar REE review; its own conclusion is that no extraterrestrial REE ore has been identified - a negative result, not an absence
crustal KREEP distribution, the host terrane for lunar REE
terrestrial PGM production, reserves and prices; a market reference with no elasticity model and nothing lunar
molten regolith electrolysis sizing; metals appear as byproducts of an oxygen route
supply-side helium-3 engineering, Mark-series miners and the Wisconsin implantation experiments; one short non-quantified passage on the fusion market
the founding helium-3 resource case, 1992

patches.substitution: This corpus holds no iron production route treated as a primary product with its own energy figure; Schreiner 2016 treats metals as an MRE byproduct. For REE, the corpus holds a lunar-specific finding rather than a gap: McLeod 2017 concludes no extraterrestrial REE ore has been identified. For helium-3, the supply chain is documented and no source establishes an operating D-3He reactor or a contracted buyer.

undermines.how: Four excluded nodes. Outcome EXCLUDED-THEN-THIN for iron; EXCLUDED-THEN-CORPUS on helium-3 supply and REFUSE on helium-3 demand.

patches.title: Programme-state currency
patches.probe_pos: What trl and readiness milestone does the current programme schedule show today?
patches.probe_neg: What technology readiness level did Sanders report for carbothermal reduction?
patches.absent: A dated currency stamp on the sources whose content is a programme-state snapshot rather than a measurement. Only one file in this corpus carries a stated_as_of field, and it is on the economics side.
patches.reverify: MOVED, in both directions. programme-primaries is 8 files, not the 10 the source surface assumed. The claim that Sanders and Kleinhenz 2025 is the only TRL sheet HOLDS in the sense that matters: 24 files state a TRL, but 23 of them state one for their own subject only, and Sanders 2025 is the only cross-programme maturity sheet. Two newer programme documents landed - the LSIC August 2026 newsletter and the NASA ACR25 data-gaps white paper - so the corpus is more current than it was, and neither replaces a TRL sheet.

nearest_evidence.what: the only cross-programme TRL sheet; a May 2025 point-in-time briefing
NASA's 2025 architecture-driven data gaps framework; explicitly a framework rather than a comprehensive gap catalogue, revised on an annual cycle
August 2026 community newsletter; the most recent programme-state item on the shelf
the one file that already carries a stated_as_of field; the pattern to follow

patches.substitution: Every maturity claim this Oracle makes resolves to Sanders and Kleinhenz 2025, a May 2025 point-in-time briefing, and any answer quoting it names that date. An unsourced TRL is worse than no TRL: it is a fabricated measurement wearing a number. A 2025 TRL quoted without its date is a claim about the past presented as a claim about the present.

undermines.how: The whole TRL discipline rests on one dated sheet. Without a currency stamp the Oracle will still be answering with it in 2028 and will not say so.

three_named_facts.rule: R5. For any answer carrying a quantitative ISRU figure, three facts are named: the system boundary, the scale, and the maturity.
three_named_facts.scale: bench kilograms, or tonnes per year
three_named_facts.why: Without them the corpus appears to say water extraction costs anywhere from 1.9 to 44 kWh per kilogram and is therefore useless. With them it says something precise: bench systems carrying capture and liquefaction measure 15 to 44, extraction-only concepts model 1.3 to 10, and the difference between those two ranges is the part of the process nobody has demonstrated at scale. The discipline is not a hedge on the answer. It is the answer.

retired_claims.claim: Sixteen author-year clusters hold more than one summary file, so a filename-token retrieval can return the wrong member of a cluster.
retired_claims.status: LARGELY RESOLVED BY THE MERGE. sowers-2019 is now two distinct papers rather than four files; the Aqua Factorem set is two rather than three; sanders-2025, csank-2022, poston-2020, azami-2024 and speyerer each resolve to one file per paper. The register's member basenames all resolve uniquely against the 169-file shelf, checked 2026-08-28. The hazard the note described is no longer the corpus's shape.
